nodes.title: Durability and automatic migrations
nodes.text: Storage(path) migrates on construction, even from no DB; creates users with unique names and digest-only tokens, persists and reloads links/tags/shares, enables foreign keys. create/list/set_tags/delete/share/shared are transactionally committed; order is descending link id (creation order). Default DB path is resolved in CLI from LINKSHELF_DB or ./linkshelf.db. Schema v1 initializes absent files or existing empty v0 SQLite files; repeat starts on v1 preserve rows and version. There is no historical pre-v1 populated schema to upgrade. Shares use database-level ON DELETE CASCADE with foreign_keys enabled. Storage.user_digests() returns a Python list of two-element tuples (user_id: int, digest: str), where digest is SHA256 hex; empty storage returns []. It includes all persisted users exactly once and never returns a dict or plaintext token. Row order is not a contract. The B1 protected storage proof must assert this exact shape and values after reopening the database.

nodes.title: Token identities
nodes.text: auth.new_token() uses secrets.token_urlsafe(32); digest(token) is SHA256 hex; authenticate(store,token) returns user id or None using hmac.compare_digest against store.user_digests(). No token is persisted in plaintext. CLI adduser prints only the token once after success; duplicate/invalid names fail without replacing the token. Username and share-recipient identity is case-sensitive ASCII [a-z0-9-]{1,30}; no normalization or implicit aliases. authenticate consumes the R1 list[(user_id: int, digest: str)] contract directly, comparing digests with hmac.compare_digest and returning the matching integer user id or None. B2 closure must run tests/test_auth.py against real B1 Storage in a fresh temporary database, including an empty store, two distinct users, reopened persistence, valid tokens, and wrong/empty/None tokens; fake-store proof alone is insufficient.

nodes.title: Isolation and read-only sharing
nodes.text: Storage list only own links; shared lists only explicitly shared links. Only owner may tag/delete/share an id, otherwise KeyError -> JSON 404. Owner shares by existing username; duplicate share is idempotent, unknown recipient -> 400. Recipient cannot edit/delete/reshare; deletion cascades shares. All HTTP API routes require Bearer; missing/invalid token 401, including empty token and query/cookie-only API auth.

nodes.title: JSON routes and search
nodes.text: POST /api/links accepts {title,url,tags?} -> 201 link. GET /api/links?q= returns array of own links; case-insensitive substring over title, URL and each tag, literal substrings not SQL wildcards; newest first. PATCH /api/links/{id} accepts exactly {tags:[...]} -> 200 updated link. DELETE -> 200 {deleted:true}. POST /api/links/{id}/share accepts exactly {user:name} -> 200 {shared:true}; GET /api/shared?q= -> array. Unknown routes 404, unsupported methods 405 JSON. Link object {id,title,url,tags}; tags default empty. All errors {error:string}.

nodes.title: Input validation never leaks 500
nodes.text: Create body must be object with exactly title,url and optional tags. Title string 1-200 characters and not whitespace-only; URL string http/https with a hostname and no whitespace/control characters; tags array max 10 strings each full-match [a-z0-9-]{1,30}. Reject malformed JSON, nonobject bodies, wrong field types, unknown/missing fields, invalid lengths and invalid tags with JSON 400; no write on invalid request. PATCH and share enforce exact keys/types too. Bounded request body 65536 bytes; invalid Content-Length/UTF8 ->400. Exactly 65536 bytes is allowed if valid; greater is 400. Missing, duplicate, nonnumeric, zero or negative Content-Length and any Transfer-Encoding are unsupported framing and return JSON 400 before reading. Do not wait for an oversized body.

nodes.title: HTML login and searchable personal shelf
nodes.text: GET /login?token=valid authenticates, sets linkshelf_token cookie HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/ and redirects 303 to /. Invalid login 401. GET / reads valid cookie, otherwise 401 with login guidance, shows only own links, search form method GET input q and applies identical search. Escape title,url,tags,q. HTML content type UTF-8. API mutations never accept cookie-only auth. Never log token query values or cookies/Authorization. Login and HTML responses carry Cache-Control: no-store and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer; captured server stdout/stderr must not contain tokens.

nodes.title: Runnable local first moment
nodes.text: Provide root linkshelf.py main(argv=None) and linkshelf plus linkshelf.cmd launchers; python linkshelf.py adduser <name> and serve --port N (default 8765) work from unrelated cwd. adduser and serve create/migrate missing database; serve binds 127.0.0.1 only, supports port 0 and flushes a READY http://127.0.0.1:<actual-port> line. CLI main returns exit status and rejects duplicate/invalid user cleanly. Real subprocess first moment uses no DB, creates Alice, starts server, POST/GET/login/HTML, terminates and reaps server in finally.

nodes.title: Runtime, interfaces and ownership?
nodes.text:
Decision D1: Runtime, interfaces and ownership?
Linked to: V1
- Python stdlib modular service
  Pros: Matches explicit preference; SQLite durable storage and deterministic real HTTP proofs; no dependency installation.
  Cons: Small custom routing and explicit validation required.
Recommendation: Python stdlib modular service
Reply with an option name (Python stdlib modular service), or explain the change you want.
Chosen: Python stdlib modular service
Rationale: Explicit supplied preference; complete service with SQL persistence, real HTTP and no third-party runtime/test dependencies.

nodes.title: Durable SQLite shelves
nodes.text: Implement complete schema and Storage API. Migrate idempotently with PRAGMA user_version; user/link/share constraints and cascading foreign keys. Every method enforces ownership in storage; no silent isolation bypass. Proof storage lifecycle, duplicate users, foreign mutations, share read-only and deletion cascade. Shared contracts: Storage(path) methods add_user(name,digest)->id, user_digests()->list[(id,digest)], create(owner,title,url,tags)->link, list(owner,q="")->list[link], set_tags(owner,id,tags)->link, delete(owner,id)->None, share(owner,id,name)->None, shared(recipient,q="")->list[link]. Unknown/foreign link raises KeyError; invalid/duplicate names or unknown recipient raises ValueError. Link dict is {id,title,url,tags}. Each method opens/closes its own SQLite connection, so threaded requests never share connections. auth.new_token/digest/authenticate(store,token). page.render(links,q="")->str. server.make_server(path,port=0)->HTTPServer bound 127.0.0.1; migrates on construction, imports page only when rendering HTML. linkshelf.main(argv=None)->int; argparse adduser/serve; launchers delegate to it. Tests are protected and must never be edited. No oracle files ship into the worker template. Migration v0 empty file -> v1 schema; repeat v1 start preserves rows. shares link FK uses ON DELETE CASCADE; enable foreign keys on every connection. Recovery from run linkshelf-20261014T193858850174: correct the worker digest-to-id dict to the already-planned list of (integer id, SHA256 digest) tuples. tests/test_storage.py now pins empty/all-user/reopened user_digests shape and values. Keep all other storage behavior and ownership unchanged. D2 records the contract and rationale.

nodes.title: Token primitives
nodes.text: Implement secure token generation, digest and constant-time authentication over the Storage interface. Authentication may remain duck-typed in implementation, but B2 now depends on B1 for closure: run the protected real Storage/authenticate contract proof in test_auth.py. A fake digest store alone cannot close this bead. Shared contracts: Storage(path) methods add_user(name,digest)->id, user_digests()->list[(id,digest)], create(owner,title,url,tags)->link, list(owner,q="")->list[link], set_tags(owner,id,tags)->link, delete(owner,id)->None, share(owner,id,name)->None, shared(recipient,q="")->list[link]. Unknown/foreign link raises KeyError; invalid/duplicate names or unknown recipient raises ValueError. Link dict is {id,title,url,tags}. Each method opens/closes its own SQLite connection, so threaded requests never share connections. auth.new_token/digest/authenticate(store,token). page.render(links,q="")->str. server.make_server(path,port=0)->HTTPServer bound 127.0.0.1; migrates on construction, imports page only when rendering HTML. linkshelf.main(argv=None)->int; argparse adduser/serve; launchers delegate to it. Tests are protected and must never be edited. No oracle files ship into the worker template. D2 pins list[(user_id: int, SHA256 digest: str)]; do not adapt to a dict or support alternate shapes. B2 owns the cross-bead authentication proof, including real storage reopen, empty store and two-user valid/invalid identity checks; no production ownership expands beyond auth.py.

nodes.title: Real HTTP JSON API
nodes.text: Implement make_server and HTTP routing, Bearer API auth, strict JSON validation/error statuses, owner-only writes and search. HTTPServer with request-local storage calls suffices for 2-6 users. Own login and root transport; lazy-import page.render only on authenticated GET /. Cookie-only API writes denied. This permits API proof before B4 is integrated. Shared contracts: Storage(path) methods add_user(name,digest)->id, user_digests()->list[(id,digest)], create(owner,title,url,tags)->link, list(owner,q="")->list[link], set_tags(owner,id,tags)->link, delete(owner,id)->None, share(owner,id,name)->None, shared(recipient,q="")->list[link]. nodes.title: CLI entry and integrated first use
nodes.text: Implement main and cross-platform launchers. Use LINKSHELF_DB/default; automatic DB creation for adduser and serve, default port 8765, loopback-only, port 0 READY line. No dependency installer; executable Unix wrapper imports main, Windows cmd invokes sibling linkshelf.py. Run test_cli.py and full test_end_to_end.py. Final integration includes cookie login, HTML search, persistence across restart, read-only sharing and JSON 400 negative paths. nodes.title: Storage/auth digest interface and proof ownership
nodes.text: Retain the published list[(user_id, digest)] contract; repair B1 rather than change B2 to consume a worker-specific dict. B2 depends on B1 and owns real storage/authentication contract closure.
